source: MAFF General Directorate of Agriculture, banana cultivation techniques manual, 2019, section VI (post-harvest notes)
text: Where a harvested bunch needs to be moved some distance for sale, it should be transported soon after cutting to a shaded washing/handling area. For fruit destined for higher-value or export markets, the general handling flow is: after separating hands from the bunch, dip or wash the fruit in water to remove the sticky latex/sap that oozes from the fresh cut surface, since this sap can stain the skin and attract dirt or mold if left on; sort/grade the fruit by size and quality; and then pack into cartons or boxes lined appropriately to protect the fruit and preserve a clean, uniform presentation. Careful washing and grading at this stage both improve the visual quality of the fruit and help reduce the risk of surface contamination that could otherwise lead to spoilage or disease development in storage and transit.
